comparison_scope: Every word, mathematical sign, index, punctuation mark, writing state, display, insertion, cancellation and marginal element was compared against the image, both C and H, and the consolidated page. changes.scan_shows: The pi-shaped sign has a flat cap, a straight left leg and a right leg curving into a low continuation towards the zero. Its surrounding words identify the vertices as the components of the fibres. The later definition separately names the acting group Pi_0 as Pi_1(C,x_0). These two locally specified roles should not be merged by a page-wide rule that every pi-shaped glyph is capital. The case is read as lowercase pi here, with medium graphic confidence; no underlying mathematical assertion is changed.
changes.apparatus_action: Withdraw existing 092-02 as a substantive C/H error: both witnesses already have the accepted pi_0. Retain its prior row/history with an explicit withdrawal and exclusion from error totals. Revise the upper-insertion inventory text and qualify the first-reading all-capitals hand/notation claim. This audit correction is to the consolidation, not a new witness error.

confirmed_doubts.reason: The small upper-right sign is an oblique stem with a short lateral branch. It still does not discriminate a reduced star from a prime; the first-display alternative order is retained.

The separate target in the explanatory insertion is retraced at its top and upper right. The heavier patch does not yield an independently recoverable earlier sign. Star/prime remains unresolved here despite the two clear stars in the body.

A longer compressed group is struck through before the live factorisant. Its left curves and taller right stroke favour soit over ce, but the stroke crosses the letter bodies, so the preferred word remains doubtful.
The final small mark after the ornate C reaches the dark right boundary. A period is plausible, but the edge prevents confident delimitation; H’s closing parenthesis is not independently established.
The initial descending y-like trace and final de-like group survive beneath the cancellation. The middle low strokes cannot establish every word, so y en a un de remains a tentative reconstruction.

The isolated point at far right is visible beyond the end of the horizontal cancellation. Its presence is secure, but its membership in the cancelled clause rather than the surviving text is still not settled.

The parenthetical group has compressed ascenders and a descending final loop consistent with abrég. The ink does not securely isolate its terminal point or every letter. No independent cancellation across the parenthesis is established; retain it live and doubtful.

A separate blackened x-like cluster precedes the live x_i. Its lower-right material is entangled with the crossing, so an earlier index cannot be recovered independently. Retain the doubtful deleted x.

A cap with descending strokes, a small lower one-like stroke, and a following open curve are visible through the hatching. The opening curve supports the retained parenthesis, but the crossed expression remains doubtful as a whole.

After the initial esp-like letters there are additional small low strokes that could form ace. They could also be the compressed abbreviation ending, so neither espace nor esp. is secure enough to remove the alternative.
The h and following low om-like run are visible. A separate period after that run cannot be confidently distinguished from its terminal stroke; retain hom|hom.
The last g has a large descending loop and a short upper terminal. A separate following point is not securely isolated; retain g|g. rather than normalize the abbreviation.

notes: Only the upper component-functor case is proposed for correction. All twelve existing doubts, including deleted text and punctuation, remain explicitly unresolved; neither agreement of witnesses nor mathematical plausibility settles the damaged ink.
The opening arrow has a clear right-pointing head; the upper annotation and factorisation use blunt horizontal joining strokes. These distinct written shapes remain as consolidated.
The baseline x_0 before son image, the raised revient au and sommet, and the raised fibre notation were checked separately. The literal two-stroke equals sign in revient au = is retained.
The unusual written phrase action de tilde C and the abbreviated il f et s. are preserved. No full words or missing hypotheses have been supplied from interpretation.
The underbrace belongs only beneath the quotient. Its four-line annotation, the colon before partir, and the unfinished final de son are all retained without completion.

All twenty inventory elements were found, including the archive folio 91 in thinner, lighter writing by another unnamed hand. No author page number is visible. H’s editorial page identification is excluded from substantive comparison.
